claim: GameXPeptides are made by entomopathogenic Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus to kill insect prey
quote:
we study the
non-ribosomal GameXPeptides, which entomopathogenic bacteria use to
kill their insect prey

claim: Traditional codon-based tests for selection do not work on NRPS because diversity comes from recombination of large DNA stretches
quote:
Traditional tests for
selection are based on changes in individual codons14,15 not recombinations of large stretches of DNA, making them unsuitable for NRPS.

claim: Rampant recombination gives each recombined stretch its own history, so one alignment yields phylogenies reflecting no part of the gene
quote:
Conflicting histories within one alignment can lead to phylogenies
that do not accurately reflect the history of any part of the gene16.

claim: NRP families are historically defined by structural similarity rather than common descent
quote:
families of NRP
are historically defined by structural similarity, not common descent.

claim: Each nematode is colonized by a few XP that grow to around 100 cells, a bottleneck expected to cause drift
quote:
each nematode of the genera Steinernema and
Heterorhabditis is colonized by a few XP, which then grow to around
100 cells

claim: The TE-domain was used as the phylogenetic yardstick because it usually occurs once per NRPS and showed no recombinations in GxpS
quote: could not identify any recombinations in TE-domains from GxpS.

claim: A tree of TTE-domains from 54 putative GxpS orthologues was inferred, rooted with the related NRPS KolS
quote:
We inferred a tree of TTE-domains (T5- and TE-domains) of
54 putative GxpS orthologues

claim: The T-domain was added to the TE-domain because it gave more sequence information and better congruence with species and domain trees
quote:
We added the T-domain to
the TE-domain because it added more sequence information and
led to better congruence to the species and individual domain trees
overall.

claim: Gene-tree-species-tree reconciliation indicated GxpS first arose in Photorhabdus and was transferred to Xenorhabdus twice
quote:
indicated that GxpS first
arose in Photorhabdus and was subsequently transferred to Xenorhabdus twice

claim: The PAPA operon was present in the LCA of XP, lost twice in Xenorhabdus, then reacquired in X. doucetiae by HGT but is probably inactive
quote:
The operon was lost twice in different groups
of Xenorhabdus and then reacquired in Xenorhabdus doucetiae via
HGT.

claim: In Xenorhabdus sp. PB62.4 the A3 domain is sister to its own A2 domain, implying A2 overwrote A3 and changed specificity from Phe to Leu
quote:
instead of grouping with
other A3 domains, the A3 domain of the GxpS of Xenorhabdus sp.
PB62.4 is sister to its own A2 domain

claim: In total 17 A-domain recombinations were found
quote: In total, we found 17 A-domain recombinations.

claim: A multitree mixture model on an A3/A5 alignment revealed at least two phylogenetic histories, one congruent with the TTE tree
quote:
This revealed that this alignment
is indeed described by at least two different phylogenetic histories

claim: Disentangling the A3 clade uncovered five more NRP-altering recombinations, each confirmed experimentally
quote:
Overall, we discovered five
more NRP-altering recombinations

claim: XtpS evolved by recombination with a foreign NRPS whose A-domain recombined with flanking regions of A4 and A5, excising A4TC4A5
quote:
XtpS evolved via recombination
with a foreign NRPS, whose A-domain recombined with the flanking
regions of the A4 and A5 domains of GxpS, leading to the excision of
A4TC4A5 domains

claim: The six-modular Gamehexpeptide synthetase arose by a TCA deletion plus an ATC duplication and an ATC insertion
quote:
The origin of the six-modular
Gamehexpeptide synthetase (HexS) involved a TCA deletion, an ATC
duplication, as well as an ATC insertion

claim: Ten unique GxpS variants with product spectra differing from the canonical orthologue were identified, predicting at least 12 new main products
quote:
Overall, we identified ten unique variants of GxpS that we predicted
to have a product spectrum different from the canonical ortholog

claim: Feeding and co-injection experiments detected 49 compounds including side products
quote: we detected 49 compounds including side products

claim: All phenylalanine-incorporating synthetases could also incorporate PAPA and mPAPA, which usually became the dominant product
quote:
found that all
phenylalanine-incorporating synthetases can also incorporate PAPA
and mPAPA

claim: Where the PAPA operon is absent but an Phe-incorporating A3 domain is present, GXPA is the main product
quote: a phenylalanine-incorporating A3 domain, GXPA is the main product

claim: Some five-modular NRPS made cyclic tetrapeptides, which are extremely rare in nature, defying the phylogenetic prediction
quote:
what makes this case unusual is that cyclic tetrapeptides are extremely
rare in nature31

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in the fifth T-domain and the TE-domain still gave cyclic tetrapeptides, consistent with cyclization by the recombined C4 domain
quote:
This still resulted in the production of cyclic tetrapeptides, consistent
with cyclization by the recombined C4 domain.

claim: Replacing the recombined C4 domain with the synthetase's own LCL-C2 domain gave only cyclic pentapeptides
quote:
This resulted in only cyclic pentapeptides, confirming that the ability to produce cyclic tetrapeptides is encoded in the
recombined C4 domain of these synthetases

claim: The resurrected LCA of all GxpS produced peptide 1, cyclo(d-Val, l-Leu, d-Phe, d-Leu and l-Leu), as its main product
quote: This revealed that the ancestral main product was 1 (cyclo(d-Val, l-Leu, d-Phe, d-Leu and l-Leu))

claim: An alternative, much less likely reconstruction differing at 244 amino acid positions also produced peptide 1
quote:
which differed from AncGxpS at 244 amino
acid positions

claim: The ancestral phenylalanine at position three was independently replaced by leucine seven times, convergently yielding four NRPS producing peptide 6
quote:
The ancestral phenylalanine at position three was independently replaced with
leucine via recombination in the A3 domain seven times.

claim: Twelve independent recombinations introduced valine-specific A-domains, giving five convergent origins of peptide 4
quote: Moreover, 12 independent recombinations introduced A-domains

claim: Four-modular GxpS evolved twice independently, and tetrapeptide production arose by three distinct mechanisms
quote:
One instance are four-modular GxpS which evolved twice
independently

claim: 27 synonymous recombination events were found against 26 non-synonymous ones, implying an important role for drift
quote: Overall, we found 27 synonymous recombination events, compared with 26 non-synonymous ones

claim: Homotypic recombinations between same-specificity domains are synonymous for the peptide and serve as the neutral proxy
quote:
We
refer to such recombinations as homotypic and they are synonymous
with respect to the NRP

claim: Homotypic recombinations are mostly very short, heterotypic ones longer, spanning whole domains or modules
quote: Homotypic recombinations are mostly very short, whereas heterotypic ones are on average longer and can span entire domains or modules

claim: Homotypic recombinations cluster in the middle of the A- and C-domains; heterotypic are more pronounced in the CA-linker and the end of the A-domain
quote:
Homotypic recombinations occur all over
the CAT-tridomain and are more frequent in the middle of the A-domain
and in the middle of the C-domain.

claim: Heterotypic recombinations hit the specificity pocket much more often than homotypic ones, a significant excess interpreted as selection
quote:
heterotypic recombinations hit the
specificity pocket much more often than homotypic recombinations.

claim: Insecticidal activity was measured for eight GXP against four insect species, and AIC chose the model giving each peptide-insect pair its own activity
quote:
The AIC chose the most complex
model, which assigns a unique activity to each peptide–insect combination.

claim: Peptide 36 was most active against S. exigua but among the least effective against P. xylostella, which was best killed by peptide 4
quote:
36 is the most active peptide against S. exigua, but
one of the least effective peptides against P. xylostella

claim: T. molitor and F. occidentalis were overall less susceptible, but F. occidentalis was killed best by 1, 6 and 10 and least by 4
quote:
T. molitor and F. occidentalis
were overall less susceptible to GXP

claim: For each insect several peptides had similar potencies, leaving room for neutral drift through equally active variants
quote:
we find that for each insect there are
several peptides with similar potencies.

claim: Actual recombination donors were significantly more similar to the recipient than same-specificity A-domains from other nrpS genes, while same-gene alternatives were equally similar
quote:
Domains from other nrpS, however, are significantly
less similar to the recipient compared with the real donor

claim: Most recombinations had donor and recipient within GxpS, with few introducing domains from other nrpS
quote:
we find that for most recombinations
in our dataset, both the donor and recipient come from within GxpS,
with only a few recombinations introducing domains from different
nrpS

claim: The bias is self-reinforcing: each within-gene recombination homogenizes sequences and raises the chance of further within-gene recombination
quote:
each recombination event between GxpS domains
homogenizes sequences within the gene and further increases the
likelihood of future recombinations between these domains

claim: NRPS can theoretically incorporate up to 300 different amino acids, but most of that alphabet is practically inaccessible to a given NRPS
quote:
NRPS
can theoretically incorporate up to 300 different amino acids38.

claim: Conventional protein evolution is less constrained because every position is a few point mutations from any proteinogenic amino acid
quote:
every position in a normal protein is at most a few point mutations
away from every other proteinogenic amino acid

claim: Each recombination overwrites one sequence and its historical record, so much of ancient NRPS history is probably lost
quote:
each recombination obliterates a small part of the history of these
enzymes, as one sequence and its historical record is overwritten
completely by another
